findings.why: The 1174 keyframe was the Cliopatria 1177 shape, ahead of the ledger (Hama and Homs 'By 1175', Sanaa 1175, Hadramawt 1180, Karak 1187) and the ledger lacked Cyrenaica ('conquered Cyrenaica before 1174'). The Hejaz (about 1,300 cells) is still drawn direct in the keyframe because the ledger only has a vassal_start there and the page gives no year for it, so a smaller snap should remain.

changes: republic-of-indonesia: ledger 8 (Dec 1948 loss, Operation Kraai): counterpart dutch-east-indies replaced by the name 'Dutch forces in Operation Kraai (Dutch East Indies)'
findings.why: The Dutch East Indies dossier's December 1948 gain (its ledger/105) is narrower than this loss, and a loss whose counterpart carries a gain in the same year is applied only as that gain; the Republic kept about 4,250 cells until its 1949 keyframe dropped 3,466 to nobody before the Dutch keyframe could take them, so the 27 December 1949 transfer handed over nothing. As a loss to a named party the cells pass through nobody's land and the Dutch East Indies 1949 keyframe takes them, then reach this state at the dissolve. Not run through the compiler.

changes: french-west-africa: ledger 10 (1922 gain of Niger): counterpart nobody -> french-africa
findings.why: The french-africa dossier (Cliopatria French Africa) already held Niger's 4,456 cells, so the gain from nobody took nothing and the 1922 keyframe added all of Niger in one jump.

changes: spanish-empire: 74 keyframes 1609-1878 (ok became adjust where needed): subtract the Cotabato Valley (admin-1 Maguindanao, Cotabato, Sultan Kudarat) in the 69 keyframes up to 1860, and Buayan's core (South Cotabato, General Santos) in all 74
